title: Smoothness versus flatness
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of
locally finite presentation.
Then $f$ is smooth if and only if $f$
is flat and every fibre $X_s$ is smooth over $\kappa(s)$.

proof.text: Apply the existing smoothness criterion to the morphism f. It states that smoothness is equivalent to flatness, local finite presentation, and smoothness of every fibre over the residue field. Since local finite presentation is an assumption of this item, the middle conjunct is redundant, leaving exactly the stated equivalence.
